newsitem.title: USA: W. Va. Supreme Court to hear trust fund appeal.
newsitem.headline: W. Va. Supreme Court to hear trust fund appeal.

text.p: West Virginia's Supreme Court has agreed to hear an appeal of a ruling that lawmakers illegally created a $3.75 billion trust fund to invest state pension money in the stock market, a court clerk said Thursday.
The court has agreed to expedite the case and scheduled oral arguments for Feb 25, the clerk said.

West Virginia's constitution bars equity investment of state money. Acting under guidelines set in a previous state supreme court ruling, the legislature created an independent entity, the West Virginia Trust Fund, in 1995 to invest state worker compensation and pension fund money.

Attorney General Darrell McGraw sued to block the investments. Kanawha County Circuit Judge Lyn Ranson ruled in October that the fund was illegally created and that such investments could only be authorized by a constitutional amendment, which requires voter approval.
Trust fund officials appealed the ruling, but agreed not to buy any stocks until the litigation is resolved.
Mark Asaad, general counsel for the trust fund, said he would argue that the lower court erred by framing the argument as strictly a constitutional question.

"There were other issues that need to be addressed, such as the establishment of irrevokable trust, the actual ownership of the various types of funds -- both employer and employee contributions," Assad said.

He said he would also argue that fund overseers would be held to a higher standard of fiduciary responsibility under the trust arrangement than if they merely followed the previously used list of state-approved investments.
West Virginia is the only state that still prohibits equity investment of public funds.
